identity: Analytic philosopher and logician · United Kingdom · 1872–1970
title: Bertrand Russell's birth chart
metaDescription: Bertrand Russell's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 27.8° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Five of the nine placements whose signs are settled stand in Taurus — the Sun, Mercury, Venus, Mars and Pluto. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 27.8° Taurus. That falls in the third decan, 20°–30°, sub-ruled by Saturn in the classical scheme — an earth sign read through a fixed season.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 3.2° Taurus, Venus was at 11.9° Taurus, Mars was at 27.6° Taurus. Read together: a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; taste for the substantial and the lasting; drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun and Uranus hold the closest angle here — a sextile, 0.2° wide. A sextile pays out only on effort; the scheme calls it opportunity rather than gift. Behind it, the Sun conjunction Mars at 0.2°, and Mars sextile Uranus at 0.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Jupiter opposes Saturn while both square Neptune. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment. The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, four sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Venus in Taurus at 11.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Taurus at 27.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Cancer at 25.6° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Capricorn at 21.0° is in domicile. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 6 in earth, 2 in water, 1 in fire by element, 5 fixed, 4 cardinal by modality. Earth weights a chart toward the material and the durable — what can be built, kept, and relied on. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Saturn was retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Virgo into Libra during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.0° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
